title: Continuum Coulomb hardness with binary nuclear charges
main_claim: Approximating inf Spec of the clamped-nucleus N-electron Coulomb Hamiltonian in R^3 (all spin sectors, full antisymmetric continuum space), with binary-encoded positive integer charges, rational positions and unary N, is QMA-hard under deterministic poly-time many-one reductions, with threshold separation b-a >= 1. The chain is: CMP square-lattice Heisenberg source, then the Piddock-Montanaro positive singlet gadget, then a half-filled Hubbard model via superexchange, then hydrogenic wells at charge scale Z_* ~ e^D, with secondary nuclei tuning the well energies to -1/2 and site displacements calibrating the hoppings.
coverage:
I read all six sections in full and re-derived the following.
(1) Lemma 1.2, the second-order bottom-energy bound, line by line.
(2) Prop 1.3 (positive-spin gadget): the singlet compressions, the effective term J_e h - (3/2)v_e^2, the error 27V^3/sqrt(Delta), and the choice of Delta.
(3) Prop 1.6 (Hubbard): the singlet hop norm 4t^2, the exchange (t^2/U)(h-I), the error 16 eta^3 R^3/U^2 <= alpha gamma/64 given the stated eta, and the floor/rounding error. U=5/8 confirmed with sympy.
(4) The contact classification distances, case by case, including horizontal vs vertical ancillas and consecutive gadgets.
(5) The right-inverse formulas, including the spoke vectors and the sign sigma, plus the 6m bound.
(6) Sec 2: the energy expansion and bracketing margins, with f(1), f(4) and the -f' bounds checked numerically; the secant and other-site slopes; the contraction theta = Cm/D^2; the Ritz cutoff and Taylor error budget (e^{-.58D}, giving bias e^{-1.16D} below eps_D = 2^{-8D/5} = e^{-1.109D}); the determinant mass lower bound K_M; the matrix perturbation tau; and the bisection and tuning error e^{-1.01D}.
(7) Sec 3: the residual identity for f = e^{-r+F}, where d_r F = W cancels the field; the barrier e^{+-g} signs and the boundary matching at r=10 and r=3D; the surrogate error m^2/D; the hole-kernel comparison; the reference bounds and displacement law, including the transverse-excess identity |w|^2/(|v|-z); positive quadrature with exact radial weights; and the orientation identity.
(8) Sec 4: the residual, Gram and matrix-entry exponents (checked .85635, 1.7127, 1.38 numerically); the IMS complement gap; the Hardy and kinetic-trace bound on Ran Pi; the many-body square completion (error 2 beta^2/c, which survives the factor Z_*); the Coulomb coefficient replacement m^5/D; and the dilation identity H/Z_*^2 = dGamma(h) + W/Z_*.
(9) Sec 5: Z_* via a truncated exponential series; the budget 3/64 + 1/64 = 1/16; the affine thresholds, with error 5/64 < 1/8 and b-a = Z_* alpha delta_s/2 exactly; and the order of construction (surrogate fields used before tuning, so the dependence is not circular).
I did not re-derive the analytic-regularity recurrence (Lemma 2.5) beyond its structure, nor the exact-inertia bit-growth claims, which are standard.
sibling_notes: There were no prior entries in family 275. The paper cites the companion UnitCoulomb2026 (unit-charge hardness) only for comparison; it does not use it, so there is no circular dependence. UniformExcessCharge2026 is cited for scope only.
